transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess what really made me come in is... I just can't shake this feeling I've been having at work. I'm a buyer, and lately, I've been thinking that people at my job, and even some of the vendors I deal with, are tracking my buys. It feels like they're messing with the launch numbers just to make me look stupid. My supervisor has sat down with me and shown me the reports, and he says they don't prove anything like that is happening, but... I just can't get past it. It feels real to me.
How long have you been having these thoughts and feelings about being tracked and targeted at work?

I'd say it's been roughly ten months now. That's how long I've been dealing with these suspicious feelings about people at work, and... well, it's also how long I've been hearing the voice, too. They both started around the same time.
Can you tell me more about the voice you hear—what does it say, and does it talk about what you're doing or comment on your actions?

It's a man's voice. I usually hear it when I'm by myself, like if I'm in the stockroom at work or driving back from a vendor meeting. It sounds like he's right behind me. He'll say things like, "Move faster, Scott," or he'll just laugh at the picks I've made for the store. I always turn around to see who it is, but... there's never anybody there.

Over these past ten months, have you noticed changes in your day-to-day functioning—like withdrawing from friends or family, losing interest in things you used to enjoy, or trouble keeping up with your usual routines and self-care?

Yeah, I have. Um, on my days off, I mostly just sit around my apartment. I'll spend time just scrolling through sneaker drops on my phone, but I don't really care about them anymore. I'm just kind of staring at it. 

And with my friends... yeah, I guess I have been pulling back. They'll text me about going to play volleyball or checking out gallery nights, and I just dodge the messages. It honestly just feels like too much work to even type out an answer, let alone actually go out and do those things.
